events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. A copyist called Bae Undal sells old answers at the foot of the jade stair: forty thousand years of top papers, bound, the margins annotated by people who failed. He swears the examiners have not changed their tastes since the stair was laid.

choices.text: Buy the bundle and study the margins

effects.log: The answers are stale but the margins are gold: every failure is a lesson in what the examiners hate. You read until your eyes ache.

choices.text: Tell him the examiners want new thinking

effects.log: "So did my grandfather," says Bae Undal, and sells the bundle to the next candidate. You study your own way and feel lonelier for it.

events.text: In the Azure Isles the weather-weavers predict the exam questions every year, and are wrong every year. Gu Hwalbi has sat the Jade Examination four hundred times and failed every one. She now tutors, cheaply, from a bench by the ink market, and her students pass at a startling rate. 'I know every wrong road,' she says. 'Someone should get use of it.'

choices.text: Take her lessons

effects.log: She is merciless and funny, and by the end you can smell a bad answer in your own hand before the ink dries.

choices.text: Ask her why she keeps sitting it

effects.log: "Habit," she says, then, after a while, "my father passed it." She charges you nothing for that lesson.

events.text: A light rain, ordered by the Azure weather office for calm nerves, falls on the candidates' queue. The night before the exam your lamp oil runs out. You arrived without a house behind you, so no servant brings more. In the next room a candidate named Ryu Seonjae is still reading, and his door is open a hand's width.

choices.text: Knock and ask to share his light

effects.log: He moves his lamp to the middle of the floor without a word, and you read back to back until the drum. In the morning he lends you a brush, too.

choices.text: Read by starlight on the balcony

effects.log: The stars above the clouds are bright enough, nearly. You catch a chill and a fine line of verse.

events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. The question is posted at dawn: 'On whether the rain owes anything to the field.' The hall goes very quiet. Somewhere a candidate laughs out loud and is escorted out. You have the morning.

choices.text: Argue that it owes nothing, and the field owes it thanks

ok.log: The examiner reading your paper underlines one sentence twice. You hear later that she quoted it at dinner.

fail.log: Your argument grows clever and then lost. You finish with a paragraph you do not remember writing.

choices.text: Write plainly about a real field you knew

effects.log: It is not elegant. One old examiner, who grew up on a farming isle, gives it a mark nobody expected.

events.text: In the Azure Isles the weather-weavers predict the exam questions every year, and are wrong every year. The examination cells are cut into the cliff of the Jade Court, open to the wind, one candidate in each. In the cell beside yours someone is crying very quietly, and has been for an hour. The proctors walk past and do not look.

choices.text: Slide a note under the partition: breathe, then write one line

effects.log: The crying stops. Later a single sentence comes back under the partition: thank you. You never learn the name.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your own paper

effects.log: You finish with time to spare. The crying stops at noon, and you do not know which way it ended.

events.text: A light rain, ordered by the Azure weather office for calm nerves, falls on the candidates' queue. A steward of an old house finds you at your lodging. The house will sponsor you: robes, tutors, a name. In return you would sit the exam under the house's banner, and owe it for as long as you hold any office at all.

choices.text: Accept the name and the debt

effects.log: Doors open that were shut. The examiners know the house; the house knows you now, and will want things.

choices.text: Decline, politely

effects.log: The steward bows exactly as deep as courtesy requires and no deeper. You remain a candidate with no backing, and the hall reminds you of it.

events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. Your inkstone cracks the morning of the exam, clean in two. The ink-seller at the gate, a thin man called Pyo Gihan, has one left, and he knows exactly what it is worth this morning.

choices.text: Pay his price

effects.log: It costs a small fortune in spirit stones. The stone is excellent, and Pyo Gihan whistles all the way home.

choices.text: Haggle him down

ok.log: He laughs and lets it go for half. "You will be a minister," he says. "Remember the inkstone."

fail.log: He will not move. You end up grinding ink on the cracked half, and your first page is grey.

choices.text: Grind ink on the broken halves

effects.log: It works, more or less. The examiner remarks on your economy in a margin.

events.text: In the Azure Isles the weather-weavers predict the exam questions every year, and are wrong every year. The cranes that carry candidates to the examination isle are old and proud. Yours lands, looks at you, and will not take off again. The crane-keeper, Mother Ha, says it does this when it disapproves of a passenger's character.

choices.text: Apologise to the crane

effects.log: You apologise for nothing in particular, with feeling. The crane considers it and takes you, slowly, by the scenic way.

choices.text: Walk the cloud bridge instead

effects.log: It takes half the night. You arrive windburnt and early, and have the hall to yourself for an hour of study.

events.text: A light rain, ordered by the Azure weather office for calm nerves, falls on the candidates' queue. Halfway through the exam the proctor nods off. The candidate across the aisle, a smiling youth with an expensive brush, holds up a folded slip of paper and raises an eyebrow at you. It is very probably the answer.

choices.text: Shake your head and keep writing

effects.log: He shrugs and passes it elsewhere. Your answer is your own and slightly worse for it.

choices.text: Cough loudly enough to wake the proctor

effects.log: The proctor wakes. The slip vanishes into a sleeve. Nobody is caught, but the smiling youth stops smiling at you.

events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. In the waiting hall a group of candidates from good houses have worked out that you have none. They compliment your robe with great care, ask after your famous teachers, and wait for you to name one.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: you climbed alone

effects.log: There is a small silence. One of them, a quiet girl from a minor house, comes over afterwards and sits by you for the rest of the wait.

choices.text: Answer with a wit they will repeat

ok.log: By noon the whole hall is repeating your line, and the young lords pretend they started it.

fail.log: Your joke lands on nobody. They laugh at it anyway, which is worse.

events.text: In the Azure Isles the weather-weavers predict the exam questions every year, and are wrong every year. The librarian of the Six Jade Ministries, old Archivist Seok, lets candidates read the precedents, but only if they reshelve one cart of returns first. The cart is the size of a skiff and the returns are a thousand years late.

choices.text: Reshelve the whole cart

effects.log: It takes four days. You learn where everything is, and Seok starts saving you the good reading desk.

choices.text: Find a way around the old woman

effects.log: You borrow a friend's reading token. Seok notices in a week and closes the stacks to you with real sorrow.

events.text: A light rain, ordered by the Azure weather office for calm nerves, falls on the candidates' queue. The exam has a verse section and you have no ear for verse. Your neighbour at the lodging, Jin Ohyang, has nothing but an ear. She offers a trade: she will drill you in metre if you drill her in law.

choices.text: Trade lessons

effects.log: Two weeks of reciting at each other across a corridor. Both of you improve. The landlord asks you to stop.

events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. An immortal named Lim Gaon has been preparing for this exam for nine thousand years, and has never sat it. He knows everything. He is always about to be ready. He offers to study with you, on the understanding that he will not be sitting it this time either.

choices.text: Study with him and ask him to sit it with you

effects.log: He knows things nobody has asked in a thousand years. On the morning, to your surprise, he comes. Whatever happens, he sat it.

choices.text: Study with him and leave him be

effects.log: He is a wonderful teacher who has never been tested. You go in alone, carrying half of what he knows.

events.text: In the Azure Isles the weather-weavers predict the exam questions every year, and are wrong every year. A pedlar works the exam queue selling luck charms: a carp scale for memory, a cloud-pine needle for calm, a dried frog for reasons he will not explain. He says the frog has a very good record.

choices.text: Buy the frog

effects.log: It does nothing that you can measure. It does make the candidate next to you laugh for the first time in a week.

choices.text: Buy nothing and say so

effects.log: The pedlar tells the queue you will fail. The queue, nervous, half believes him.

events.text: A light rain, ordered by the Azure weather office for calm nerves, falls on the candidates' queue. A letter arrives from a village below the clouds, from the people who knew you before you climbed. Inside are dried persimmons and a note in a hand you do not know: the children are all saying you will be a minister. Nobody has told them what a minister is.

choices.text: Write back before the exam

effects.log: You write about the jade stair and the cranes, and leave out the exam. You sleep better than you have in a month.

choices.text: Keep the persimmons for the morning of the exam

effects.log: You eat them in the cell at noon. The taste of a village orchard is a strange thing to have up here, and it steadies your hand.

events.text: Dawn comes up out of the eastern cloud sea, and the Azure examination hall smells of wet slate. The results go up on the jade wall. Your name is not there. A name that is almost yours, one character different, is near the top. The clerk at the wall shrugs: errors happen, and there is a form, and the form takes eleven years.

choices.text: File the form

effects.log: Eleven years later a letter apologises. It is the most patient thing you have ever done, and it teaches you how the ministries work.

choices.text: Find the examiner and argue it now

ok.log: The examiner checks the paper, goes pale, and corrects the wall by hand while you watch.

fail.log: The examiner hears you out and files you under nuisance. You will sit it again.

events.text: The Azure clerks keep the weather ledgers: every shower an isle is owed, and every one it has had. The rain ledger of a fishing isle in {cth_realm} is out by one storm. One storm, owed for six hundred years. Your senior, Clerk Bang Jiwol, says correcting it would mean reopening six hundred years of accounts, and lunch is soon.

choices.text: Reopen the accounts

effects.log: It takes a decade. The fishing isle gets its storm, and sends you a dried fish the size of a door.

choices.text: Note it for later and go to lunch

effects.log: Bang Jiwol buys the dumplings. The isle stays dry. You think about it more than you expected to.

events.text: A drizzle someone forgot to cancel has been falling on the Azure archive roof for a century. A petitioner waits on the bench: an old tide-spirit named Ullim, whose isle drifted out of {cth_realm} in a gale and into a neighbour's waters. The neighbour now taxes it. He has been waiting four years for someone to read his petition.

choices.text: Read it now and take it upstairs

effects.log: Your superior grumbles but signs. The isle is towed back by cloud whales. Ullim cries, which for a tide-spirit is mostly salt.

choices.text: Put it on top of the pile

effects.log: It is read in a month instead of four years. Ullim says that is the kindest thing a ministry has ever done for him.

events.text: In the Azure ministry, the windows face the sea of dawn and nobody works before it is fully up. Your new desk comes with a seal nobody can explain. It is old, it is heavy, and it is listed in the inventory as 'the seal'. Clerk Moon Hyeok warns you never to use it, and cannot say why.

choices.text: Find out what it seals

effects.log: Three months in the archive. It seals pardons for one particular isle, which nobody has asked for in ten thousand years. You keep it oiled.

choices.text: Use it as a paperweight

effects.log: It is a very good paperweight. Nothing happens, and you never learn what nothing cost.

events.text: The Azure clerks keep the weather ledgers: every shower an isle is owed, and every one it has had. Yun Pallo, the senior clerk at the desk beside yours, has been asleep for thirty years. Everyone works around him. His in-tray is a small tower. You have been told, kindly, that he does his best work later.

choices.text: Do his tray quietly

choices.text: Leave a cushion under his head and get on with your own

effects.log: He wakes at last with the cushion and no idea who to thank. The office calls you thoughtful.

events.text: A drizzle someone forgot to cancel has been falling on the Azure archive roof for a century. The ministry tea is terrible and has been for twenty thousand years. It is bought on a contract nobody can find, from a supplier nobody has met. Every clerk drinks it and complains. You could look into it.

choices.text: Look into it

effects.log: The supplier turns out to be a minister's cousin, now retired, still paid. The tea improves; the minister does not forgive you.

choices.text: Bring your own and say nothing

effects.log: You drink good tea alone and feel faintly treacherous.

events.text: In the Azure ministry, the windows face the sea of dawn and nobody works before it is fully up. A merchant named Hong Daesu leaves a lacquer box on your desk while you are out. Inside are spirit stones, a good many, and a card hoping your review of his trading licence will be swift and kind. He did not sign it, which is almost honest.

choices.text: Send it back with the licence unreviewed

effects.log: He comes in person to apologise and is so pleasant you nearly like him. His licence is reviewed like everyone's.

choices.text: Keep it and review him swiftly

effects.log: The review is swift and kind. The stones are good. You find you dislike the sight of lacquer boxes.

choices.text: Report it to the censor

effects.log: Hong Daesu is fined. The other clerks are careful around you now, which is both a compliment and not.

effects.log: The archive looks like a laundry and smells worse. You save most of it, including an old decree that will matter later.

events.text: A drizzle someone forgot to cancel has been falling on the Azure archive roof for a century. An order crosses your desk, sealed and correct: clear the village off a small isle so the isle can be moved for a pleasure garden. It is lawful. It is signed by someone far above you. The village has two hundred people and a school.

choices.text: Stamp it. It is lawful

effects.log: The village is moved, with compensation that does not buy a school. The garden is lovely. You do not visit.

choices.text: Find a flaw in its form and send it back

ok.log: A missing countersign. The order goes back for correction and, slowly, is forgotten.

fail.log: There is no flaw. It returns with a sharp note about your diligence.

choices.text: Unseal what she sealed before anyone notices

effects.log: You stay late with a knife and steam. Ahn Soyul owes you, and says so for a hundred years.

choices.text: Help carry them to the roof

effects.log: The inspector is delighted. It rains that night. Some of the petitions are now unreadable, and so is Do Hanbit's face.

choices.text: Wear last year's faded robe instead

effects.log: You look poor and correct. The master of ceremonies nods to you, which is rare.

events.text: In the Azure ministry, the windows face the sea of dawn and nobody works before it is fully up. At the ministry banquet the seating is by house, and you have no house. Your place is at the end of the last table, near the kitchen door, beside the junior archivist and a draught.

choices.text: Enjoy the kitchen door

effects.log: The cooks send out the best of everything to the end table first. You eat better than the ministers and hear all the gossip.

choices.text: Ask the steward to seat you by rank

effects.log: He does, stiffly. You sit among people of your rank who are all from houses, and they look at you like a stain.

choices.text: Help him carry his things to the crane

effects.log: Nine boxes of letters and one of dried peony seeds. He gives you a packet. They grow.

events.text: The Azure lords speak softly, the way people do who can hear thunder coming a month off. Two factions of {cth_court} have invited you to dinner on the same night. One is led by the Minister of Rites, who loves order; the other by the Minister of Revenue, who loves numbers. Whichever you attend, the other will remember for an age.

choices.text: Dine with the Minister of Rites

effects.log: Seven courses served in an order older than your family. You are now, in the eyes of the court, a person of ceremony.

choices.text: Dine with the Minister of Revenue

effects.log: He talks about the spirit stone tithe until midnight and is never once boring. You are now a person of numbers.

choices.text: Send apologies to both and dine alone

effects.log: Neither forgives you, but both respect it. You eat noodles and read.

events.text: High in the Azure court, policy is argued the way weather is made: slowly, then all at once. {cth_ruler} asks you, in a quiet moment after audience, what you honestly think of the Minister of War. Everyone in the hall has stopped breathing. The Minister of War is standing twelve paces away.

choices.text: Tell the truth, briefly and kindly

effects.log: You say he is brave and bad with supply. The Minister of War hears it, and after a cold year he asks you to look at his supply.

choices.text: Praise him without reserve

effects.log: {cth_ruler} looks at you a little longer than is comfortable, and asks no more questions of you that season.

events.text: High in the Azure court, policy is argued the way weather is made: slowly, then all at once. Below the clouds a mortal realm under the care of {cth_realm} is starving after three failed harvests. Opening the spirit-rice granaries would save it. It would also empty the reserve the ministry keeps for wars.

choices.text: Open the granaries

effects.log: Spirit rice goes down the cloud stairs in a river of carts. A mortal kingdom names a festival after you, and the Minister of War never quite forgives you.

choices.text: Open half

effects.log: Half is enough to save most of it. Everyone is a little unhappy, which is called policy.

choices.text: Keep the reserve

effects.log: Two years later a war comes and the reserve is needed. You were right. It does not feel like it.

choices.text: Sit for him honestly

choices.text: Ask him to flatter you, and pay for it

choices.text: Lean, quietly, toward the most capable

effects.log: You choose the dull, capable one. If they win, you rise. If not, you will be remembered.

choices.text: Seat them by age and let age take the blame

effects.log: The elder is pleased and the younger is told to wait. They both find this very proper.

choices.text: Keep it

effects.log: It is printed. {cth_ruler} reads the passage and laughs once, and the ministry looks foolish. You have made an enemy at Rites.

events.text: In the Azure Isles a poem is read first from a cliff, so the sea of dawn can have the first hearing. The widow of a cloud soldier asks you for a poem to be read at her husband's funeral. She did not know him well, she says; it was an arranged match, and she wants something true, not grand.

choices.text: Ask her about the small things

effects.log: You learn that he whistled badly and fixed things nobody asked him to. You write that. The whole funeral laughs and cries.

choices.text: Write something grand and fine

effects.log: It is a beautiful poem about duty. She thanks you. You suspect it was not what she wanted.

choices.text: Give it honestly, with what is alive in it first

effects.log: She cries, then takes notes, then comes back in ten years with something that makes you jealous.

choices.text: Praise it to spare her

effects.log: She glows and publishes it as it is. It is mocked, and she does not write again for a long time.

events.text: In the Azure Isles a poem is read first from a cliff, so the sea of dawn can have the first hearing. A thousand-year work of yours, half finished, has been lost: a servant used the scrolls to light a brazier on a cold night. The servant, a boy named Duri, is waiting to be punished and has brought his own switch.

choices.text: Send him away with nothing but a warning

effects.log: You write the work again from memory. It is better. Duri brings you tea for a hundred years.

choices.text: Dock his wages

effects.log: Fair, and he takes it. The work is gone. You start something else, a little colder.

events.text: At the Azure barracks the morning drum is struck when the sun clears the cloud sea, not before. Drill on the parade isle of {cth_legion}: formation flying on cloud skiffs, fifty abreast, in a crosswind. Sergeant Pi Gyeongsu shouts at everyone equally. Your skiff has a wobble.

choices.text: Hold the line anyway

ok.log: You hold it. Pi Gyeongsu says nothing to you, which is high praise.

fail.log: The wobble wins and you peel off into a cloud. You are on latrine duty for a month.

choices.text: Report the wobble and ask for a new skiff

effects.log: The quartermaster sighs and fixes it. The squad learns that it is permitted to report things.

events.text: The Azure wing of the Cloud Legion drills inside fog banks, so its soldiers learn to fight by ear. A young cloud soldier, Yun Daram, is caught slipping away on a supply skiff at night. He says his mother's isle is drifting into a storm and nobody will give him leave. The penalty is a black mark and a year on the punishment isle.

choices.text: Speak for him to the captain

effects.log: The captain gives him three days' leave and you three days of his duties. He comes back. His mother's isle is saved.

choices.text: Let the penalty stand

effects.log: He takes the mark. He serves well afterwards, and never speaks to you again.

events.text: The Azure wing of the Cloud Legion drills inside fog banks, so its soldiers learn to fight by ear. Night watch on the outer isle, in a storm. Your watch partner, an old soldier called Gong Jaeil, has fallen asleep standing up. Something is moving out in the clouds, too far off to make out.

choices.text: Wake him and signal the fort

effects.log: It is a drifting merchant hulk, empty. The captain still praises the watch.

choices.text: Go out alone and look

ok.log: It is a lost cloud whale calf. You guide it home with a lantern. The legion talks about it for a year.

fail.log: You lose the isle in the storm and are found at dawn, frozen, by a patrol.

effects.log: The fortress holds for another age, empty. A lesser garrison closes the strait.

effects.log: Nothing breaks. Junyeol leaves for the capital.

events.text: Azure titled houses dress in the colours of the day's sky; a dinner of them looks like a forecast. The peers of {cth_realm} meet once a millennium in the Hall of Titles. As {cth_title}, you have a seat. The custom is that the newest peer pours the wine for all the others, on their knees, for the whole night.

choices.text: Pour, and remember every face

effects.log: By dawn your knees ache and you know who drinks too much, who refuses and who thanks the pourer. It is the most useful night of your career.

choices.text: Pour once, then hand the jug to a servant

effects.log: A gasp. Half the peers think you arrogant. The other half have wanted to do that for ten thousand years.

events.text: The Azure nobility measure their age in storms remembered, and lose count politely. An old house proposes an alliance: their heir is to marry into your household, joining your new title to their ancient name. Their heir, Lord Seol Jaewon, is pleasant and has the ancient name's ancient debts.

effects.log: The ancient name opens doors. The debts open your coffers.

choices.text: Decline with a gift

effects.log: The house is offended and then relieved: they had another offer. You keep your coffers.

events.text: Azure titled houses dress in the colours of the day's sky; a dinner of them looks like a forecast. A peer of an old house, Lord Mun Taegeuk, has challenged your right to your title under a rule from the age of the first stair. The challenge is settled by a bout with blunted swords in the Hall of Titles.

choices.text: Accept the bout

ok.log: You win it cleanly. Mun Taegeuk bows, and buys you dinner, and becomes a friend of sorts.

fail.log: You lose it, with dignity. The rule says you may keep the title if the hall agrees; the hall, grudgingly, agrees.

choices.text: Answer with a lawyer instead

effects.log: Your lawyer finds the rule was repealed, eleven thousand years ago, in a footnote. Mun Taegeuk is mocked.

A ruined old house of {cth_realm} has one surviving member: a proud, threadbare woman named Lady Baek Ilha, who will sell her family's ancestral hall to pay her debts. The new rich are bidding. choices.text: Buy it and let her keep living there

choices.text: Let the market have it

effects.log: A spice merchant buys it and paints it red. Lady Baek moves to a small isle and writes rude letters to everyone.

events.text: The Azure throne faces the sea of dawn, and every audience begins when the light reaches the steps. The first audience of the day at {cth_throne}: a farmer from a small isle has walked the jade stair for three months to complain about a tax collector. The tax collector is here too, with his house's lawyer.

choices.text: Hear the farmer first

effects.log: The farmer is clear and brief. The lawyer is neither. You rule for the farmer, and the whole court hears that you did.

choices.text: Send it to the ministry

effects.log: Proper. The farmer walks home three more months.

A case is brought to the throne: a poor immortal, Gu Yeongsu, stole spirit rice from a granary to feed a village below the clouds in a famine. The law says exile. choices.text: Pardon him and reform the famine law

effects.log: A long, satisfying argument with the ministers. The law changes. Gu Yeongsu becomes the keeper of the granary.

choices.text: Uphold the law and commute the exile

effects.log: He serves a short sentence. The court thinks you firm but fair.

choices.text: Uphold the law

effects.log: He is exiled. The court approves. The village does not.

effects.log: Two plotters plot again. Most people think you magnificent. Your guard captain thinks you mad.

choices.text: Free all but the plotters

effects.log: The amnesty is grand and safe. The plotters' families petition, sadly.

events.text: Your Azure audience hall is cool and damp, and petitioners bring umbrellas out of respect. The Ministry of Works proposes a monument to your reign: a statue of you on the highest isle of {cth_realm}, visible from every strait. It would take ten thousand workers a century.

events.text: From the Azure throne you can order a rain, and find out afterwards whom it fell on. The court censor, the unbribable Master Ha Seongjun, has submitted a memorial criticising your spending on the palace gardens. He is right. The memorial is public, and the whole court is waiting to see what you do.

effects.log: The gardens grow wild and lovely by themselves. The censor is surprised into a smile.

effects.log: The court learns that thanks are free.

events.text: The Azure throne faces the sea of dawn, and every audience begins when the light reaches the steps. One of your consorts, Lady Yeo Haneul, has been writing letters to a lord at the court of {cth_foe}. Your spymaster has the letters. They are about birdwatching. Probably.

choices.text: Ask her about it, plainly

effects.log: She is mortified: the lord is her brother, estranged. You arrange a meeting. They weep and quarrel about birds.

choices.text: Have her watched

effects.log: She is watched for a century. It is about birds. She knows she was watched.

events.text: Your Azure audience hall is cool and damp, and petitioners bring umbrellas out of respect. The court asks you to name an heir to {cth_throne}. You have three candidates, none of them your own kin: a capable general, a gentle minister and a sharp young magistrate who reminds you of yourself.

choices.text: Name the gentle minister

effects.log: The court sighs with relief. The general sulks. The magistrate studies harder.

choices.text: Name the magistrate

effects.log: The court is startled. The magistrate does not sleep for a week, then sets to work.

choices.text: Name no one yet

effects.log: The court keeps guessing, and guessing is a kind of work.

Bai Yeonok, the best embroiderer of {cth_realm}, will do it for nothing, if you promise that her home isle will not be taxed for an age after you win.

choices.text: Promise

effects.log: She sews it in a month: the finest banner in the sky. You have made your first promise as something more than a rebel.

choices.text: Pay her instead

effects.log: She takes the money. The banner is good, not great.

events.text: In the Azure Isles a rising begins with a change in the wind, and the weather-weavers notice first. Volunteers for the rising arrive at your hidden isle every night: farmers, rogues with no backing, a few cloud soldiers who have deserted {cth_legion}. Your quartermaster, a calm woman called Pak Sunok, says you cannot feed them all.

choices.text: Take them all and ration

effects.log: A hungry army is still an army. They learn to share.

choices.text: Take only those who can fight

effects.log: A lean army. The turned-away farmers go home and tell their neighbours.

choices.text: Trust her and look elsewhere

effects.log: You look elsewhere and find the spy: it was Ho Minjun himself. The cook goes on making soup.

effects.log: Safe, and a little cruel. They teach your soldiers bookkeeping.

events.text: In the Azure Isles a rising begins with a change in the wind, and the weather-weavers notice first. Midway through the rising, your oldest follower, the white-haired former marshal Cheon Mugeol, asks you one question in private: 'When you have the throne, what will you do on the first morning?'

choices.text: Tell him truthfully

effects.log: You tell him. He nods. You are not sure what he thinks. He stays.

choices.text: Say you have not thought about it

effects.log: "Think," he says. "Before the morning comes." You do, for nights.

A boy from the village below your isle, Dohyeon, wants you to teach him to read the old court script. He wants to sit the Jade Examination one day. choices.text: Send him to a proper tutor, and pay

effects.log: He gets a proper tutor and passes sooner. He sends you nothing; he never knew.

effects.log: You wait, and miss nothing. The planning was a festival.

events.text: From the Azure throne you can order a rain, and find out afterwards whom it fell on. Two isles of {cth_realm} petition the throne on the same day: one for rain for its rice, the other for sun for its salt pans. They are next to each other, and the weather cannot be cut in half.

choices.text: Order a narrow rain, exactly on the border

ok.log: The weather-weavers manage it, sweating. Rice on one side, salt on the other. The court calls it a miracle of policy.

fail.log: The rain wanders. Both isles are half wet and fully cross.

choices.text: Alternate them by month

effects.log: Neither isle is happy. Both survive. That is most of ruling.

effects.log: Nine nephews and Dal. Dal wins. It takes a month and the court gains weight.

choices.text: Buy, and beat the foe to it

effects.log: The mine is yours. The families are paid off, and leave.

effects.log: Proper, and her court takes it as a slight.

events.text: At the candidates' lodging below the jade stair, a thin, quick girl named Ryu Gaeun is copying model answers by lamplight onto silk fine enough to sew into a sleeve. She sees you see. 'Paek Juhwan pays me,' she says. 'His house is rich and his father thinks him a fool. I have a mother below the clouds and no money at all. What would you do?'

choices.text: Offer to study with her so she can sit it herself

effects.log: You study together every night for a month. She stops copying for Paek halfway through, and he does not know yet.

choices.text: Tell her you will not keep it secret

effects.log: She goes white and says nothing. In the morning the silk is gone from her table, and so is she, for a day.

choices.text: Say it is not your business, and go to bed

effects.log: It is not your business. You lie awake anyway and listen to her brush going until dawn.

events.text: The morning of the Jade Examination. Two rows ahead of you Paek Juhwan, handsome and pale, eases back his left sleeve to write, and there is silk inside it. Proctor Hwang Seori, who has kept this hall clean for nine thousand years and is proud of it, is walking down your row, slowly.

choices.text: Catch the proctor's eye and look at the sleeve

effects.log: Hwang Seori does not stop walking. She simply stands beside Paek Juhwan until the end of the exam, and his brush never moves again.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your own paper

effects.log: You write the best answer of your life and do not look up once. Paek Juhwan finishes early.

choices.text: Afterwards, tell Paek quietly that you saw

ok.log: He hears you out, shaking, and withdraws his paper that afternoon. Nobody knows why but the two of you.

fail.log: He laughs in your face. "Prove it," he says, and you cannot.

events.text: The season after the examination, Lord Paek Hyeonsu, Juhwan's father, sends for you. He is a big, tired man in a small cold room full of ledgers. 'My son tells me you know something about him,' he says. 'So does half the hall, it seems. I want to know what you mean to do with it. I would also like to know why he thought he needed to cheat.'

choices.text: Tell him: because his father thinks him a fool

effects.log: He is silent for a long time. "I did think it," he says at last. "I will try to stop." It is the strangest apology you have ever witnessed.

choices.text: Tell him you mean to do nothing

effects.log: He nods slowly and offers you a post in his house. You decline it. He respects that more.

choices.text: Ask what it is worth to him

effects.log: He pays without blinking. You leave richer, with a patron who will never trust you.

events.text: Years later Ryu Gaeun's name goes up on the jade wall: she sat the Jade Examination under her own name and passed, near the top. She finds you in a tea house to tell you. 'Paek Juhwan paid my fee,' she says. 'No note. He keeps a lighthouse on a far isle now, and they say he likes it. Do you think I should write to him?'

choices.text: Tell her to write

effects.log: She writes. He writes back, at length, about gulls. They write to each other for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Tell her to let it lie

effects.log: She lets it lie. You wonder sometimes whether you were right.

events.text: Proctor Hwang Seori retires after nine thousand years and sends for you: she has a small house on a cloud and a great deal of tea. 'You were the only candidate in all that time who looked at me instead of at the question,' she says. 'Most cheats are caught by someone who cares more about the hall than the answer. That is a kind of answer too.'

choices.text: Ask her about the other cheats she caught

effects.log: She tells you nine thousand years of stories, and you learn more about the court from them than from any book.

choices.text: Pour her tea and say nothing

effects.log: You drink tea together until the light goes. She gives you her proctor's seal to keep.

fail.log: He laughs in your face. "Prove it," he says, and you cannot.

events.text: The season after the examination, Lord Paek Hyeonsu, Juhwan's father, sends for you. He is a big, tired man in a small cold room full of ledgers. 'My son tells me you know something about him,' he says. 'So does half the hall, it seems. I want to know what you mean to do with it. I would also like to know why he thought he needed to cheat.'

choices.text: Tell him: because his father thinks him a fool

effects.log: He is silent for a long time. "I did think it," he says at last. "I will try to stop." It is the strangest apology you have ever witnessed.

choices.text: Tell him you mean to do nothing

effects.log: He nods slowly and offers you a post in his house. You decline it. He respects that more.

choices.text: Ask what it is worth to him

effects.log: He pays without blinking. You leave richer, with a patron who will never trust you.

events.text: Years later Ryu Gaeun's name goes up on the jade wall: she sat the Jade Examination under her own name and passed, near the top. She finds you in a tea house to tell you. 'Paek Juhwan paid my fee,' she says. 'No note. He keeps a lighthouse on a far isle now, and they say he likes it. Do you think I should write to him?'

choices.text: Tell her to write

effects.log: She writes. He writes back, at length, about gulls. They write to each other for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Tell her to let it lie

effects.log: She lets it lie. You wonder sometimes whether you were right.

events.text: Proctor Hwang Seori retires after nine thousand years and sends for you: she has a small house on a cloud and a great deal of tea. 'You were the only candidate in all that time who looked at me instead of at the question,' she says. 'Most cheats are caught by someone who cares more about the hall than the answer. That is a kind of answer too.'

choices.text: Ask her about the other cheats she caught

effects.log: She tells you nine thousand years of stories, and you learn more about the court from them than from any book.

choices.text: Pour her tea and say nothing

effects.log: You drink tea together until the light goes. She gives you her proctor's seal to keep.

events.text: Minister Do Gyeongmun of Revenue, who lifted you out of the ranks when you had no house behind you, is accused of hiding a spirit vein's whole income for a thousand years. Censor Gi Hyang, who has never once been bribed and is proud of it, wants your testimony on the minister's ledgers. You kept some of them. You know they do not add up.

choices.text: Testify honestly

effects.log: You tell Gi Hyang exactly what you saw. It is not much, and it is enough. Do Gyeongmun sends you no message at all.

choices.text: Refuse to testify against your patron

effects.log: Gi Hyang writes your name in a small book. The court notes your loyalty, and some of it notes it against you.

choices.text: Speak for his character, and say nothing of the ledgers

effects.log: You praise him at length and tell no lies. Gi Hyang looks at you as if you were a ledger yourself.

events.text: Ahn Biryeo, Do Gyeongmun's secretary for six thousand years, comes to your door at night with a box. 'His true books,' she says. The hidden income went, every stone of it, to an isle of children orphaned in the last Isle War, which the court would not fund. Unlawful. Kind. 'He would rather fall than see them moved,' she says. 'I would rather he did not fall.'

choices.text: Give the books to the censor

effects.log: Gi Hyang reads them all night. In the morning the charge is changed: not theft, but disobedience. It is still a fall.

choices.text: Hide the box and keep his secret

effects.log: The box goes under your floor. The orphans' isle stays hidden, and you have joined the crime.

choices.text: Send the books to the throne directly

effects.log: A bold road around the censors. The throne will know before the court does, and the censors will never forgive it.

events.text: The hearing before {cth_ruler}. Do Gyeongmun, old and very straight, confesses to everything before anyone has asked: the vein, the thousand years, the lies. He names no isle and no children. He looks at you only once, across the hall, as if to say: do not. Censor Gi Hyang is watching you too.

choices.text: Speak for him: tell the throne where the money went

ok.log: The hall goes still. {cth_ruler} sends for the orphans' records, reads them, and turns the sentence into exile with honour.

fail.log: The throne hears you and is unmoved: law is law. Do Gyeongmun closes his eyes.

choices.text: Do as he asks and keep silent

effects.log: He is stripped of rank. The orphans' isle is never mentioned. He nods to you as they lead him out.

choices.text: Ask for mercy without saying why

effects.log: Mercy without reasons is a small thing at court. He is exiled to a far orchard isle, not a quarry.

events.text: Do Gyeongmun's ministry needs a minister. The post of Revenue, with its seal and its ledgers and his old chair, is offered to you. Ahn Biryeo is still there, keeping the files. The orphans' isle, found or not, still needs feeding every season, and the treasury has never once wanted to feed it.

choices.text: Take the post and fund the isle openly

effects.log: You put the orphans' isle in the budget under its own name. The council argues for a year and passes it by two votes.

choices.text: Take the post and change nothing

effects.log: The ledgers are clean now. The isle quietly starts to go hungry, and Ahn Biryeo stops speaking to you.

choices.text: Decline the post

effects.log: It goes to {cth_rival}. Ahn Biryeo resigns and goes to the orchard isle to keep the old man's books.

events.text: Censor Gi Hyang comes to your office after many years, with a bottle of something old. 'You were the only one who told me the truth,' says the most feared official at court. 'Everyone else told me what they thought I wanted.' He pours. 'Do Gyeongmun writes to me, you know. About his orchard. I think he forgave us both.'

choices.text: Drink to the old man

effects.log: You drink to him, then to the orphans' isle, then to the truth, and the censor sings, badly.

choices.text: Ask the censor who is next

effects.log: He smiles, very slightly, and tells you. You spend the next century making sure it is done fairly.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: You are named regent of {cth_throne} for a child sovereign named Haneul, who is small even for an immortal child and wants above all things to fly a kite off the highest terrace. Old Mokran, the child's nurse, holds Haneul's hand at the ceremony. Lord Gwak Taesan, the child's uncle, who expected the regency himself, smiles at you warmly across the hall.

choices.text: Promise the child, before the court, to give the seal back

effects.log: Haneul nods solemnly and asks how many years. You say: when you are ready. The court writes it down.

choices.text: Ask Old Mokran to raise the child away from audiences

effects.log: Haneul flies kites and learns letters in the gardens. The court sees the child seldom, and sees you a great deal.

choices.text: Seat the child beside you at every audience

effects.log: Haneul is bored and fidgets and listens to everything. The court sees the throne and the regent together.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: Lord Gwak Taesan proposes, kindly, that the child be sent for safety to his own isle, far from the dangers of court, until of age. The proposal has the support of half the regency council. Old Mokran catches your sleeve in a corridor. 'If Haneul goes to that isle,' she says, 'Haneul will not come back.'

choices.text: Refuse, and keep the child at court

effects.log: Gwak Taesan bows and withdraws his proposal. He does not withdraw his smile.

choices.text: Outmanoeuvre him in council

ok.log: You propose instead that Gwak Taesan be honoured with a post on the far border. The council, relieved, agrees.

fail.log: The council splits. Nothing is decided, and Gwak Taesan has learned what you will do.

choices.text: Agree, and send Old Mokran with the child

effects.log: The child goes. Old Mokran writes to you every month, and her letters grow shorter.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: Haneul has gone missing from the palace. The guards are searching every terrace. You find the child at last at the cloud harbour, sitting on a crate with three old fishermen, mending a torn kite with fishing twine and eating dried squid. Haneul looks up at you and says, very clearly, 'I do not want to be a throne.'

choices.text: Sit on the crate and help mend the kite

effects.log: You mend the kite. The fishermen tell you which winds are best. Haneul goes home holding your hand, and asks to come back.

choices.text: Tell the child the truth about what a throne is

effects.log: You say it is mostly listening to people. Haneul thinks about this and decides that perhaps it can be done.

choices.text: Have the guards bring the child home

effects.log: Haneul goes home without a word. The kite stays on the crate.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: A decree appears in Haneul's own careful hand, sealed with the child's seal: it names Lord Gwak Taesan sole regent. The hand is perfect. Haneul, shown it, bursts into tears and says it was never written. Old Mokran says the child spent an afternoon last month practising letters with the uncle.

choices.text: Expose the forgery before the whole court

effects.log: Gwak Taesan is stripped of his titles. The court is shaken, and it trusts the regency more.

choices.text: Send Gwak Taesan quietly to a far isle

effects.log: No scandal. He goes. Some of his friends at court never learn why, and wonder about you.

choices.text: Let Haneul decide what to do with the uncle

effects.log: Haneul thinks for a long time and says: send him somewhere with no paper. The court laughs, and remembers.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: Haneul is grown: tall now, and quick, and still fond of kites. The day of the handover comes. The regent's seal of {cth_throne} sits in your hand for the last morning, as heavy as it was the first. Haneul waits at the top of the jade stair. Old Mokran, very old now, is in the front row, crying already.

choices.text: Hand over the seal at once and step down the stair

effects.log: You hand it over and walk down the stair, and the court sees a regent who kept the promise. Haneul does not let you go far.

choices.text: Hand it over and stay on as an advisor

effects.log: Haneul asks you to stay. You stay. The court wonders who rules, and Haneul shows them, slowly.

choices.text: Ask for one more year

effects.log: One more year. Haneul agrees, coolly. The court does not forget it, and nor does Haneul.

events.arc: The Child on the Jade Throne
events.text: Old Mokran is gone, peacefully, in her sleep. Haneul, on the throne now, asks you to speak at her funeral, because you were the one who kept the child at court when it mattered. The whole palace comes: the cooks, the gardeners, the fishermen from the harbour with a kite.

choices.text: Speak about the day she caught your sleeve

effects.log: You tell it plainly. Haneul hears for the first time how close it was. The fishermen fly the kite off the terrace afterwards.

choices.text: Let Haneul speak, and stand beside

effects.log: Haneul speaks, stumbles, and finishes. You stand at the throne's shoulder, where you have always been.

events.text: Yeo Damin is the best weaver in {cth_realm}, and she will make the banner of your rising herself, on one condition. Her younger brother Yeo Jun was sent to a quarry isle for a debt he did not owe, and has been cutting stone there for three hundred years. 'Bring him home,' she says, 'and I will weave you a banner the whole sky will look up at.'

choices.text: Promise to bring him home

effects.log: She starts weaving that night. You have made the first promise of the rising.

choices.text: Tell her the rising cannot spare soldiers for one man

effects.log: She weaves the banner anyway, slowly, and does not look at you while she does it.

events.text: The quarry isle: a grey rock in a cold strait, two hundred prisoners, and forty tired guards who have not been paid in a year. Yeo Jun is somewhere among the prisoners. Your lieutenant, Marshal Seo Dongha, a white-bearded old soldier who resigned from {cth_legion} to join you, thinks the guards can be bought.

choices.text: Take the isle by night

ok.log: You are over the wall before the guards wake. Not one of them is hurt. Two hundred prisoners walk out, Yeo Jun among them.

fail.log: The guards wake. You get out with half the prisoners and a wound, and Yeo Jun is not among them.

choices.text: Pay the guards their missing year

effects.log: They take the stones and open the gate. Some of them join you. Yeo Jun walks out blinking.

events.text: A cloud bridge at dusk, under a flag of truce. Captain Im Gyeol of the guard of {cth_throne}, whom you once drank with in a better age, comes alone. 'The north gate of the palace isle is mine,' Im Gyeol says. 'I will open it on one night, if you swear my guards walk away unharmed. Not for you. Because the throne stopped listening.'

choices.text: Swear it

effects.log: You swear on your oath token, and it does not cloud. Im Gyeol nods once and walks back across the bridge.

choices.text: Refuse: you will not take the throne by a door

effects.log: Im Gyeol looks at you a long time. "Then you will take it by a wall, and more people will be hurt." You know that is true.

choices.text: Say yes, and plan not to need it

effects.log: You say yes and mean maybe. Im Gyeol knows the difference, and says nothing.

events.text: The rising comes to the jade stair of {cth_court}. Yeo Damin's banner goes up over the isles at dawn: you can see it from every strait, as she promised, and from the throne room too. Behind you is everyone who came: farmers, rogues with no backing, deserters, Yeo Jun with a quarry hammer. Ahead is the stair, and {cth_ruler} at the top.

choices.text: Climb the stair openly, in daylight

effects.log: You climb in full view. Every isle sees it. Whatever the throne does now, it does with the whole sky watching.

choices.text: Send a last offer to parley before you climb

effects.log: The offer goes up the stair. It is answered with silence and then, after a day, with a small white flag.

choices.text: Take the stair by the north gate before the sun is high

ok.log: The palace isle is yours by noon, and the fighting is over before it starts.

fail.log: The gate is shut. The fighting is long and hard, and the banner is torn.

events.text: When it is over, one way or another, Yeo Damin finds you on the terrace with a small knife. She unpicks one red thread from the edge of the banner and ties it round your wrist. 'So you remember,' she says, 'that it was woven by people with names.' Below, her brother is asleep against a pillar.

choices.text: Keep it on, always

effects.log: You wear it for ten thousand years. People ask about it. You tell them her name, and his.

choices.text: Ask her what she wants now

effects.log: "Nothing," she says. "A loom. A small isle." You give her both, and she complains about the loom.

events.text: Captain Im Gyeol comes to you, years after the rising, out of uniform. 'Every one of my guards walked away,' the captain says. 'Every one. I did not think you would keep it. I have come to ask for work, if there is any for someone who opened a door once.'

choices.text: Make Im Gyeol captain of your own guard

effects.log: The court thinks it mad. Im Gyeol guards you for an age and never once opens a door that should be shut.

choices.text: Give the captain a quiet isle and a pension

effects.log: Im Gyeol takes it, and writes to you every spring about bees.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: You send Nam Gyuri as envoy to {cth_foe}. She is clever and curious and has wanted for a thousand years to see their star wells. Her brother Nam Seokjin, a ferryman, rows her out to the departure quay himself. On the quay he takes your arm. 'She goes where she likes,' he says. 'She always has. Promise me you will bring her back.'

choices.text: Promise him

effects.log: He lets go of your arm and rows home without looking back. You feel the promise sitting in your chest like a stone.

choices.text: Tell him you cannot promise that

effects.log: He nods. "Nobody can," he says. "I wanted to hear someone say it." He rows away.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: Gyuri's letters were long and funny for two years. Then they stopped. The last says only that she has been invited to see the star wells of {cth_foe} at last, and will write when she comes back. That was a year ago. Seokjin has come to your office every week since and waits on the bench outside your door.

choices.text: Ask the court of {cth_foe} formally

effects.log: A formal question earns a formal answer: the envoy is well. It tells you nothing.

choices.text: Send a second envoy quietly to find her

effects.log: Your second envoy, a quiet clerk named Bok Sunam, goes to look. It will be a year.

choices.text: Bring Seokjin in from the bench and tell him everything

effects.log: He listens and says thank you. After that he waits inside, and brings you tea.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: A woman in plain travelling clothes asks for you at night: Lady Hwa Yeon, of the court of {cth_foe}. 'Your envoy is alive,' she says, 'kept very comfortably in a pavilion by the star wells. She found an old map in our archive. It shows the isle this war began over was claimed by a forgery. My house's forgery. Some of my court would like that map to vanish, and her with it.'

choices.text: Negotiate for her release through Lady Hwa

ok.log: Lady Hwa agrees to carry a letter, and a promise of silence about the map, back to her court.

fail.log: Lady Hwa listens and goes, promising nothing.

choices.text: Offer a trade: the map stays hidden, Gyuri comes home

effects.log: Lady Hwa considers it. "She will not like that," she says. "But I will put it to her."

choices.text: Ask why she is telling you

effects.log: "Because the map is true," says Lady Hwa, "and I am tired of my house's lies." You trust her more than your own spies.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: A letter at last, in Gyuri's quick hand: 'I am not coming back. Not because I cannot. Because I can do more here. Lady Hwa and I will bring the map to their throne together. If we are right, the war ends. If we are wrong, they will send me home in disgrace and you may say you told me so. Tell Seokjin I am well and eat too much. Tell him I am sorry.'

choices.text: Read the letter to Seokjin yourself

effects.log: He reads it twice, then a third time, then laughs: "She always does too much." He cries a little, too.

choices.text: Support her plan from your side of the border

effects.log: You start the slow work of readying your own court to hear that the war was a forgery.

choices.text: Order her home

effects.log: You send the order. She does not obey it. You knew she would not.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: The war with {cth_foe} ends over an old map. It is not quick and it is not clean, but it ends, and the isle it began over is given back by the house that forged the claim. Nam Gyuri does not come home. She is made an officer of their court, which is strange, and she writes to her brother every week.

choices.text: Go to the ferry quay and tell Seokjin it is over

effects.log: He rows you out into the middle of the strait and you both sit there until dark, looking at nothing.

choices.text: Write to Gyuri to thank her

effects.log: She writes back four scrolls about the food and one line: thank you for letting me not come back.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: Nam Seokjin comes to you in his ferryman's coat, many years later. 'You promised to bring her back,' he says, quite cheerfully. 'You did not. So I am collecting another way.' He has a ferry ticket to the court of {cth_foe}, for two. 'She has adopted a little boy. I would like you there when I meet my nephew. You owe me.'

choices.text: Go with him

effects.log: You cross the strait in his ferry, and Gyuri meets you on the quay with a small child and too much luggage, and you are forgiven entirely.

choices.text: Give him your seal as a pass instead

effects.log: He goes alone and brings back a drawing the nephew made of you from the description. It is not flattering. You frame it.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back
events.text: You send Nam Gyuri as envoy to {cth_foe}. She is clever and curious and has wanted for a thousand years to see their star wells. Her brother Nam Seokjin, a ferryman, rows her out to the departure quay himself. On the quay he takes your arm. 'She goes where she likes,' he says. 'She always has. Promise me you will bring her back.'

choices.text: Promise him

effects.log: He lets go of your arm and rows home without looking back. You feel the promise sitting in your chest like a stone.

choices.text: Tell him you cannot promise that

effects.log: He nods. "Nobody can," he says. "I wanted to hear someone say it." He rows away.

events.arc: The Envoy Who Did Not Come Back

The last says only that she has been invited to see the star wells of {cth_foe} at last, and will write when she comes back. That was a year ago. Seokjin has come to your office every week since and waits on the bench outside your door.
